parsed.main_gap: The key Lemma (that the small-prime support σ(x)=P(x)∩{p≤a_1} of every term is itself good) is asserted with 'details omitted'; it carries the entire difficulty of the problem.

errors.description: The central lemma, on which the whole finiteness/periodicity argument rests, is not proved at all. Its statement is nontrivial (the write-up itself notes the boundary problem 102/17=6<15 and alludes to an 'Rp^k' construction that is never presented). Without it the argument shows nothing beyond an easy reformulation.
errors.quote: **Proof.** Induction over the sequence terms in increasing order (standard; details omitted). \(\square\)

errors.description: The 'surviving hypothesis' paragraph gestures at a proof idea (repairing the quotient x/p by a construction Rp^k preserving the ≤A support) but gives no definition of R, no argument, and no verification that the construction yields a term; this cannot substitute for the omitted lemma proof.
errors.quote: The construction \(Rp^k\) repairs this boundary issue while preserving exactly the small-prime support; the lemma proves the strengthened hypothesis.

parsed.notes: Sections 1 and 3 are correct and cleanly written: characterization (1) of terms via 'good' prime sets, unboundedness, and the derivation of a_{n+T}=a_n+L from translation-invariance mod L. But these are routine; the entire substance is the unproved lemma. Computational evidence and hypothesis discussion earn no credit.
